clue.text: Wee onion spread round near back

indicators.note: spread round something means the scattering word is wrapped about it

parts.note: to sow seed is to spread it over the ground

indicators.note: turned back, the word for near is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: by means near, as in standing by the door

explanation.surface: A little onion being scattered round the back of something close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' is the Scots word for small and flags a Scots answer: SYBOW is the Scottish name for a spring onion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybow (also sybo) is a Scots dialect word for the spring onion or scallion, a small young onion.

clue.text: Humperdinck's 'invention' — EH's No. 1 in charts, arranged with REM and timps

indicators.note: to arrange music is to rework it, so all these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written; EH reads as Engelbert Humperdinck the pop singer

indicators.note: the number one place in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of charts
taken as written
taken as written; timps is short for timpani

explanation.surface: Pop trivia: the singer Engelbert Humperdinck's number one hit, rearranged with a band and kettledrums.
explanation.walkthrough: Two Humperdincks: the surface means the 1960s crooner whose 'Release Me' was a No. 1, but the definition means the composer of Hansel and Gretel.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer Humperdinck introduced this half-sung, half-spoken vocal style in his opera Königskinder of 1897.

clue.text: Swarmer about to swarm? The old light up

definitions.note: 'The old' marks the verb as archaic

indicators.note: a word about another goes round it, enclosing it

parts.note: bees are the insects best known for swarming
to shin up a tree is to swarm up it, climbing with arms and legs

explanation.surface: A bee about to swarm, with the old hive lighting up.
explanation.walkthrough: Swarm has two senses: the bee swarms as a colony, while 'to swarm' is to climb, which is what shinning does.
explanation.definitionFit: Beshine is an archaic verb meaning to shine upon, illuminate.

clue.text: Live through a tough winter? This thing's unsettling

indicators.note: unsettled letters are knocked out of place; the ones left are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the letters to take out of the phrase before it

explanation.surface: Surviving a harsh winter is an unsettling experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of THING are taken out of A TOUGH WINTER and the seven left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to last longer than it, enduring until it is over, so to live through it.

clue.text: Process occurring when core of herring is encased in salt?

indicators.note: something encased in another is wrapped inside it

parts.note: Attic salt is sharp wit, so salt means wit

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: A fish-curing question: what happens when a herring's middle is packed in salt?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Process' and 'salt' both look like food curing; one is a legal summons and the other is wit.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a process is a summons or writ, the formal written order that starts or carries on an action.

clue.text: It's a doddle fringing little bed with ornamental loops

indicators.note: a fringe runs round an edge, so this word goes round the other

parts.note: something easy is pie, as in easy as pie
a cot is a small bed for a baby

explanation.surface: Trimming a baby's cot with lace loops is child's play.
explanation.walkthrough: A doddle is British slang for an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: Picoté describes lace or ribbon edged with picots, the small decorative loops of thread.

clue.text: Dried ginger in a recipe as filling for banana split coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top
a filling goes inside, so these letters go into the middle of the other word
a split word is opened in two, leaving a gap for the filling to go in

parts.note: Musa is the botanical genus of the banana
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe: dried ginger stuffed into a banana split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' is part of the instruction: the reversed banana genus is split to take A and R in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Asarum is wild ginger; its dried rootstock was used like ginger as a spice and medicine.

clue.text: Something maybe left by writer in the trenches is interesting

definitions.note: warms in the sense of stirs up interest or enthusiasm

parts.note: the trenches stand for the First World War, so this is war writing
MS is a manuscript, something a writer leaves behind

explanation.surface: A war poet's papers found in the trenches turn out to be fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue builds a WAR MS, a manuscript from the trenches; the definition is loose, taking warm as to rouse interest, so this parse is less certain than most.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm someone is to kindle their enthusiasm, so something that warms its reader is engaging their interest.

clue.text: Prayer made to god when overcome by serious breathing disorder

parts.note: ARD is acute respiratory disease, and acute means serious
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A prayer offered up during an alarming attack of breathlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'overcome by' puts AS beneath ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardas is the Sikh formal prayer of supplication, recited at the end of services and ceremonies.

clue.text: Trendy Aussie youth, not old, making the old mutter

definitions.note: 'the old' marks the verb as archaic

parts.note: a Roy is Australian slang for a trendy young man
ne is an obsolete word for not

explanation.surface: Old folk grumbling about fashionable young Australians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not, old' reads as 'no longer old', but it is one block: the archaic word for not.
explanation.definitionFit: Royne (also roin) is a Spenserian word meaning to mutter or growl.

clue.text: Primitive creature not, note, caught by old fool

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it

parts.note: mome is an old word for a fool or blockhead
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old fool catching a primitive animal, or rather not doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not, note' reads as a correction in the surface, but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotremes, the platypus and echidnas, are the most primitive living mammals, laying eggs like reptiles.

clue.text: Shifty man one's caught in lie, chiselling maybe

indicators.note: something caught in another is held inside it

parts.note: a story is a lie, as in 'don't tell stories'

indicators.note: something shifty keeps shifting, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy man is caught lying about cheating someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Chiselling is slang for cheating, which suits the shifty man; the definition takes it literally, cutting stone. The rearranged letters go in after the O of the lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonemasonry is the craft of cutting and dressing stone, and chiselling is one example of that work.

clue.text: It may make you sweat, alternative role involving your spit?

indicators.note: an alternative version of the words is a different arrangement of their letters

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, joining the letters of role

explanation.surface: A sauna or a stage part that has an actor sweating and spitting.
explanation.walkthrough: All twelve letters of 'role' and 'your spit' are rearranged together. Pleurisy root is a North American milkweed, Asclepias tuberosa, whose root was given as a medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of this plant was used as a diaphoretic, a remedy that brings on sweating, as well as for chest complaints.

clue.text: Suit carl got out in country style (rare)

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the phrase describes in the same way, as in 'a dance in country style'

indicators.note: letters that have got out of their places have broken loose and can be put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A peasant's suit, unpacked to show off a rustic fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: A carl is an old word for a churl or peasant, which suits the country picture; '(rare)' warns that this form of rustic is seldom used.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustical is a rare variant of rustic, meaning belonging to or in the manner of the countryside.

clue.text: E.g. Puerto Rican in the US involved in matter to do with bivalent metal

indicators.note: something involved in another is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: matter is an old word for pus

parts.words: E.g. Puerto Rican in the US
parts.note: in the US a Latino is a person of Latin American descent, such as a Puerto Rican

explanation.surface: A Puerto Rican living in America caught up in a chemistry question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' looks like the chemistry subject; it is the old medical word for pus.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinous describes compounds of platinum in which it has a valency of two, as opposed to platinic.

clue.text: Philosopher's method of investigating endless wild party, name-less

indicators.note: with no end, the word for a wild party loses its final letter

parts.note: an orgy is a wild, unrestrained party
anon, short for anonymous, describes something without a name

explanation.surface: A philosopher studies a nameless, never-ending wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'name-less' turns it from a deletion signal into a single word meaning anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Organon, Greek for instrument, is the title of Aristotle's logical works and means a system of rules for philosophical or scientific inquiry.

clue.text: Customer having right protected by court

indicators.note: something protected by another is shielded on both sides by it

parts.note: Ct is the abbreviation for court
a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A shopper whose consumer rights are upheld by a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like the usual R, but here it is the legal right called a lien.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is someone who buys services or goods from a professional or business, the same role as a customer.

clue.text: Some dates put back creating distress

indicators.note: putting something back here means reading it in the opposite direction
only some of the letters of the phrase that follows are used, a run lying inside it

parts.note: the run of letters inside dATES PUt

explanation.surface: Postponing a few appointments causes someone anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' reads as postponing the dates, but it also tells you to reverse the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset as a noun means a state of distress or emotional disturbance.

clue.text: A fillet

parts.note: surface reading: a boneless cut of meat or fish, as served at table
setter's reading: a fillet is also a narrow band or ribbon worn round the head

explanation.walkthrough: The two words have no wordplay; the trick is the second sense of fillet, a headband rather than a cut from the butcher. With crossings this definition alone is enough.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is a garland or chaplet for the head, and dictionaries gloss it as a fillet, the old word for a headband.

clue.text: Waxy stuff bringing back of hairstyles to the front?

indicators.note: the letter at the rear of the word is picked up and carried elsewhere
says where that rear letter goes: before all the others

parts.note: perms are permanent-wave hairstyles

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's wax product that brings the back of a style forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of PERMS moves to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperm is short for spermaceti, the white waxy substance from the head of the sperm whale, once used in candles.

clue.text: Wordy joke I established as feebler than the rest

parts.note: a pun is a joke made with words
taken as written
est. is the abbreviation for established

explanation.surface: Someone owns up that their wordplay joke is the weakest of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting for a crossword: the setter calls a pun the feeblest joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Puny means weak or feeble, so its superlative means weaker than all the others.

clue.text: Cornish mineral? Another of those turned up in lake

indicators.note: one item in another sits inside it

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word reads upward, back to front

parts.note: tin is another Cornish mineral, mined there for millennia

explanation.surface: A Cornish mineral, and another one found upturned in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another of those' points back to the definition: another Cornish mineral, the famous one.
explanation.definitionFit: Erinite is a green copper arsenate mineral, first described from specimens found in Cornwall.

clue.text: Forester especially comprehends such a measure

indicators.note: to comprehend is literally to take in, so the phrase holds the answer within it

parts.note: the run of letters inside foreSTER Especially

explanation.surface: A woodsman, of all people, understands this unit of measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such a measure' points back to the forester: the answer is a measure used for cut timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A stere is a cubic metre, used especially as a unit for measuring stacked firewood.

clue.text: Fool given obsolete operation guarantee

parts.note: an ass is a fool
ure is an obsolete word for use, practice or operation

explanation.surface: An idiot is handed a promise about some old surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: URE survives only in inure and enure; on its own it is an old word for use or working.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure is to promise confidently or make certain, which is what a guarantee does.

clue.text: Around Arkansas I pay inordinately for US gum?

indicators.note: a word around another goes round it, enclosing it
inordinately means out of order, so the letters are put in a new one

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
AR is the postal abbreviation for Arkansas

explanation.surface: A shopper in Arkansas paying too much for chewing gum.
explanation.walkthrough: In the southern US a gum is a beehive made from a hollow gum-tree log; an apiary is a place of hives, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiary is a place where bees are kept in hives, and a US gum is one such hive.

clue.text: Unctuous host after what's written up

indicators.note: the host comes after, so its piece is placed second, below the other
in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, something written
a host is an army, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: An oily host buttering up a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' here is not someone giving a party but a multitude, specifically an armed one.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes someone ingratiating and oily in manner, which is what unctuous means.

clue.text: Pregnant model burying her head? (5, two words)

indicators.note: a buried thing ends up inside, so that letter is set back within the word
the model's head, her first letter, is taken off the front

parts.note: a pin-up is a model whose picture is pinned on walls

explanation.surface: An expectant model hides her face, ostrich-like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burying her head' suggests an ostrich, but it moves the model's first letter down inside the word. The enumeration warns of two words.
explanation.definitionFit: In pup is said of a bitch carrying young, so it means pregnant.

clue.text: What was next in line is this

definitions.note: 'was' marks the word as old or dialect

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the run of letters inside liNE IS This

explanation.surface: Asking which person was next in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next in line' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the signal and 'line' starts the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Neist is an old and Scots form of next, the nearest in order.

clue.text: Murphy's rule accepted by one of his countrymen? Yes, initially

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman, as Murphy is an Irish name
r. is the abbreviation for rule

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of yes

explanation.surface: Murphy's Law, endorsed by a fellow Irishman: yes, at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murphy's rule' suggests Murphy's Law, but a murphy is slang for a potato, Ireland's staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Praty is an Irish dialect word for a potato, and murphy is a slang name for the same vegetable.

clue.text: Sisters maybe getting married in very revealing garb?

indicators.note: getting into something puts one item inside another

parts.note: minis are miniskirts, very short and revealing
m. is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Nuns marrying while wearing something very skimpy.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is nuns, of all people, in revealing garb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minims are a Roman Catholic religious order founded by St Francis of Paola, with friars and also an order of nuns; hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Commuting train i.e. scarcely moving

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the state of scarcely moving

indicators.note: to commute is to change or exchange, so these letters swap places

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A commuter's lament: the rush-hour train is barely crawling along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commuting' looks like daily travel by train; it is the signal to change the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness, a tendency to stay still or barely move at all.

clue.text: Poison: in localized areas it is swallowed by those enjoying prosperity

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside whatever swallows it

parts.note: ups are those who are up, doing well
in dialect, a is used for it, he or she

explanation.surface: A warning that the wealthy are swallowing poison in certain places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In localized areas' means in dialect: there 'a' stands for 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a Javanese tree whose milky sap was used as arrow poison, so the word came to mean poison or any baneful influence.

clue.text: Describing treacherous girl, Anacreontic about one 'speaking properly'?

indicators.note: a word about others goes round them, enclosing them

parts.note: Anacreon came from Teos, so Teian describes him and his verse
a means one
RP is Received Pronunciation, the standard accent of 'proper' English

explanation.surface: A love poem in Anacreon's manner about a two-timing girl who speaks well.
explanation.walkthrough: Anacreontic usually means amorous or convivial verse; here it simply stands for Anacreon's birthplace, Teos.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpeia was the Roman girl who betrayed the Capitol to the Sabines; Tarpeian refers to her and the rock named after her.

clue.text: Musical expression, composite, for one historically i/c roll-calls

parts.note: mus. is the abbreviation for musical
a term is a word or expression
the aster is a composite, a plant of the daisy family Compositae

explanation.surface: A composer's term, made up of parts, for an old military official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composite' looks like an adjective describing the musical expression; it is a noun, a daisy-family flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A muster-master was the officer who kept the muster roll, the register of troops called and checked at a muster.

clue.text: Do they set exams fool (in pieces) missed in Prestatyn?

definitions.note: the answer is a collective body, so 'they' fits it

indicators.note: the word for fool is not in one run, but in separate pieces within the town name
letters that are missed out are dropped from the word

parts.note: a seaside town in north Wales, taken as written
a prat is a fool

explanation.surface: A question about whether examiners sit papers in a Welsh seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: PR and AT come out of PRESTATYN separately. Estyn is the education and training inspectorate for Wales, so the Welsh setting is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Estyn inspects schools in Wales rather than setting exams, hence the question mark on the definition.

clue.text: We'll be back in inflamed spot, unpleasantly hot

indicators.note: one item in another sits inside it

parts.note: a sty is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid

indicators.note: will be back means returning, so the short word is read in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone promises to come back to a sore, uncomfortably hot spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We'll be back' sounds like a promise to return; it just sends WE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewy describes a stuffy, oppressively close heat, like being in a stew.
